extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and editors preparing or assessing submissions to European Science Editing (ESE)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and policies for preparing, submitting, and peer-reviewing manuscripts for the journal European Science Editing, including formatting, ethical, peer-review, AI, and editorial standards. Covers requirements for authors, responsibilities for reviewers, and editors' duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limits by manuscript type
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum main body word counts differ by manuscript type: Original articles and Reviews up to 4000 words; Viewpoints up to 2000 words; Correspondence up to 500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are limits for main body text only. Authors should consult the full Instructions for Authors for detailed requirements and typical headings for each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Original articles: structured abstract (Background, Objectives, Methods, Results, Conclusions) up to 250 words. Reviews: unstructured abstract up to 250 words. Viewpoints: unstructured abstract up to 100 words. Correspondence: abstract not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original articles the abstract should contain the main findings with numerical and statistical values, if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Original articles, Reviews, and Viewpoints: 4–6 keywords. Correspondence: not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Original articles and Reviews: maximum 6 tables/figures; Viewpoints: maximum 2; Correspondence: maximum 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On submission include figures in the manuscript to facilitate review; on acceptance provide high-resolution .tif or .jpg files. Tables should be in text format at the end of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page and title style
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be non-declamatory (i.e., does not give study findings) and include a study descriptor (for example, 'a cross-sectional study', 'a case study'). Title page must include author names (first and last), affiliations (institution, town/city, country), and corresponding author contact details (indicated with an asterisk and email). A manuscript should have only one corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are provided (e.g., 'Editors’ attitudes about Plan S – a cross-sectional study').

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent identifiers encouraged (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID identifiers for all authors are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID can be obtained without charge at https://orcid.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources of funding must be declared as an acknowledgment. Authors should describe the role of the study sponsor(s) in study design, data collection, analysis and interpretation, writing of the report, and decision to submit. If the funder had no involvement, state this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corresponding author should confirm they had full access to all the data and final responsibility for the decision to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of body text and typical headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Original articles: Introduction, Methods (including Statistical Methods and Ethics), Results, and Discussion (including Strengths and Limitations and Conclusions). Results and Discussion may be combined. Reviews/Viewpoints: headings as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subheadings if required, not numbered; clearly identify level 1 headings in bold and level 2 headings in bold italics (preferably using styles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (ICMJE four criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting research findings should meet all four ICMJE criteria: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design/data acquisition/analysis/interpretation; (2) drafting or revising critically for important intellectual content; (3) final approval of the version to be published; (4) agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should decide who qualifies for authorship and order before submission; editors do not adjudicate authorship and may refer irregularities to institutional ethics authorities. Use of the CRediT taxonomy is encouraged where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors should disclose any financial and personal relationships with other people or organisations, even if not directly related to the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests must be declared at the end of the manuscript just before the References section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements and funding role
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge all sources of external funding and describe the role of the funder, if applicable. Also acknowledge anyone who contributed but is not an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: References style and maximum numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations in text: consecutive superscript numbers (Vancouver style). References: list the first three authors then et al.; journal titles and page ranges in full; book and journal titles in italics. Provide DOI as a URL where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum number of references: Original articles 30; Reviews 40; Viewpoints 20; Correspondence 5. Electronic sources should include URL and date accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting: file formats, typeface, and heading markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be in .docx or .odt, preferably 12-point typeface, with page numbers. Clearly identify level 1 and level 2 headings (bold / bold italics) using text processor styles where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables should be at the end of the manuscript as separate pages; figures included in the manuscript for review and submitted as separate high-resolution files on acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and general style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use UK spelling as in the Oxford English Dictionary (including -ize and -ization where appropriate). Use inclusive language (non-sexist, non-racist). Minimize abbreviations and define at first use (except SI units and widely accepted terms). Write numbers one to nine in full except when attached to units of measure. Use double quotation marks for direct quotations and terms used out of usual context; single quotes only for quotations within quotations. Avoid redundant language and excessively complex sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to consult the EASE Guidelines and to refer to a language editor if necessary. Poorly written or organized manuscripts are less likely to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables: include at the end of the manuscript on separate pages, number consecutively, provide informative title and legend; must be in text format (not spreadsheets/images). Figures: include in the manuscript for review; on acceptance provide separate files in .tif or .jpg (high-resolution, 600 dpi, minimum width 12 cm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EASE Science Editors' Handbook chapters are referenced for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary files and reporting checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supporting data or other required files (eg reporting checklists) should be uploaded as supplementary files with associated metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit via the online submission system; complete submission forms including the EASE Interactive Checklist for Submitting Authors signed by all authors at submission. Steps include specifying manuscript type, entering metadata, classification categories, completing supporting agency/conflict/ethical details, agreeing to data publishing policy, and uploading files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author must provide contact details for all authors and confirm each co-author has approved the final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed reviewers guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally suggest up to 3 potential reviewers (full name, email, institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider diverse peer reviewers in terms of gender, ethnicity, and geographical distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint and secondary publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles already available on preprint servers or published in another language are accepted for consideration but must be declared at submission. Do not submit manuscripts whose content overlaps substantially with already published items or other manuscripts under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, authors will be requested to update pre-publication versions with a link to the final published article. Contributions based on published material should be identified and must provide original analyses or opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and similarity checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are checked for text similarity with CrossRef Similarity Check and manually reviewed to determine whether flagged text shows evidence of plagiarism. Manuscripts suspected of plagiarism will be handled following COPE flowcharts and ICMJE guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval for studies involving humans
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts reporting data from studies involving humans must provide proof of formal review and approval, or formal review and waiver, by an appropriate IRB or ethics committee; approval and its number should be reported in the Methods section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the institution lacks a formal IRB, follow the Declaration of Helsinki. State how informed consent was obtained and whether participants received compensation. Authors should not unilaterally determine exemption; cite institutional/regulatory policy. Chief Editor may ask for documentation of review and recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-sharing statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For original articles, a data-sharing statement should be included with links to the data set where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data sets are too large, authors are encouraged to upload them to FigShare, Dryad, or institutional repositories with appropriate citation. Consult ICMJE Recommendations - Data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests and conflicts disclosure procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential financial and non-financial competing interests (including relationships with editorial associations, commercial editing companies, medical communications companies, etc.) must be declared at the end of manuscript before References.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial editorial screening criteria for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts will be considered for peer review only if they are within the aims and scope of the journal, sufficiently original, have no serious scientific flaws, and have satisfactory grammar and English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection process is usually completed within 2 weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and reviewer numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is single-blind (reviewers see authors' names). Original articles: at least two independent external experts; Reviews and Viewpoints: at least one independent expert. Reviewers are usually not identified to authors but may sign their reviews optionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief Editor makes the final decision about publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should focus on the scientific quality and overall style (clear and concise academic writing) rather than thorough linguistic copyediting. They should indicate whether the manuscript is scientifically sound and coherent, how interesting it is, and whether writing quality is acceptable. Reviewers should declare any conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers spot the need for linguistic edits they should inform the Author and Subject Editor in the report. Small orthographic or stylistic errors may be corrected by reviewers during reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct during revision rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: During a second review round, reviewers may be asked to evaluate the revised version against previous comments and indicate whether concerns were addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised manuscripts must be submitted with a tracked-changes copy and a detailed response to editors' and reviewers' comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised manuscript submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit two copies of the revised manuscript: one highlighted using Word's Track Changes (not highlighting) to show changes, plus a separate detailed response to editors' and reviewers' comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide clear documentation of changes can delay further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors believe a retraction is not justified they may appeal to the Chief Editor once. Appeals will be discussed by the editorial team and, if necessary, EASE Council. For discovered substantive errors, the journal will correct the record via correction notice or retraction following JAMA recommendations and COPE guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions at the conclusion of the appeal process are final. Articles undergoing appeal may be sent for further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata, corrigenda, retraction, and expression of concern criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Errata: minor admissible errors not affecting content/scientific integrity. Corrigenda: significant errors that affect scientific integrity (e.g., authorship changes, mistakes in findings, figure/table labelling). Retractions: used when the findings are unreliable due to misconduct or honest error and to correct the literature. Expression of concern: consider when evidence of misconduct is inconclusive, findings are unreliable but institution will not investigate, investigations are unfair/inconclusive, or an investigation is underway but judgment will be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions for errata/corrigenda are with editors after discussion with authors. Retractions follow COPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and article processing charges
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal provides immediate open access; no submission or publication charges are levied on authors (diamond open access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content is distributed under Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship changes after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in the number or order of authors after original submittal must be explained in writing to the Chief Editor. Editors reserve the right to refer irregularities in authorship to the appropriate institutional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EASE and reporting guidelines (SAGER etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are advised to consult the EASE Guidelines for Authors and Translators and to follow EASE Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) guidelines where relevant (use terms sex/gender carefully).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to consult reporting checklists and include appropriate items as supplementary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — general recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, journals, and publishers should create, publish, and monitor adherence to AI policies; collect and publish declarations of AI use by journals, authors, and reviewers; and provide educational resources. AI use should be declared in appropriate manuscript sections, a separate AI declaration, or via publication facts labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should include information on raising concerns, consequences of infringement, and appeal mechanisms. Monitor adherence and provide regular reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI authorship/contributorship rule
rubrics_metrics.description: AIs should not be listed as co-authors on publications because they cannot be responsible for accuracy, integrity, and originality of the work required for authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should consider WAME, ICMJE, and STM guidance on this topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and citations/literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: AI outputs should not be cited as primary sources for backing specific claims because AI-provided citations and information can be inaccurate or fabricated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers must read and verify sources; consider time-stamping AI outputs if mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use in data collection/analysis/code generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any use of AI for data collection, cleaning, analysis, interpretation, data generation, or code generation should be disclosed in the Methods (or AI declaration) and accompanied by robustness/reliability indicators and steps to ensure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be aware of risks (e.g., fake data generation) and request appropriate disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use in visualisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any use of AI for visualization (tables, figures, images, videos) should be disclosed in Methods and in captions/legends. AI-generated visualisations may require additional validity checks and reproducibility steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may consider policies banning AI-generated visuals; examples of retractions for 'nonsensical' images are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use for writing, language, and style editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify whether and how authors should declare use of AI for writing, language, or style editing. Options include declaring such use in Acknowledgements or AI declaration, or treating it like spell-checking (no declaration needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should recognize difficulty distinguishing AI-assisted drafting vs editing; provide clear guidance to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use during peer review (reviewer guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should specify whether reviewers are allowed to use AI tools and distinguish between AI for language/style editing vs AI-created review content. Reviewers should declare any AI use in creating/editing review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should state whether they will check reports for AI authorship and what consequences follow. Some funders/publishers prohibit AI use by reviewers; bans are hard to enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy for editors and editorial staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Editors should verify AI disclosure, ensure AI tools are not listed as authors, and follow up on undeclared AI use. Editors must not upload unpublished manuscripts, confidential correspondence, editorial decisions, or review reports to generative AI tools, nor use AI for editorial evaluation and decision-making. Editors retain full responsibility for editorial assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be vigilant for irregular citation formatting, vague/generalised content, abrupt tone shifts, unrealistic visuals, and repetitive AI-like patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting AI policy adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should monitor adherence to AI policies, provide regular reports on adherence and infringements, and publish their policies and declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information on how to raise concerns and appeal decisions related to AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identification, registration, and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may sign their reports; they must declare conflicts of interest. Peer reviews can be registered with external services (e.g., Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service); reviewers will be notified and can decline registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The online submission system will send review requests and reminder notifications, and reviewers can decline via provided links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Final responsibility for editorial decisions lies with the Subject Editor and/or Editor-in-Chief. Where necessary, editors may seek advice from the Editorial Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of strong disagreement between reports, the editor may assess according to expertise or seek board advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy, copyright and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain copyright; by submitting they grant EASE a license to publish and identify itself as the original publisher. Content is distributed under CC BY 4.0. Authors must ensure submitted content does not infringe copyright; permission must be provided for reproducing copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access content is normally CC-BY; exceptions may apply. The Provider reserves the right to refuse or remove content at its discretion.
